headline: Google releases PARDIG global precipitation datasets with author-reported multi-network evaluation
summary: Google DeepMind and Google Research released PARDIG, an experimental global precipitation-estimation dataset trained on sparse NASA/JAXA GPM spaceborne radar retrievals with satellite imagery and atmospheric-field inputs. It provides 0.1° grids every 15 minutes: a near-real-time stream for 2016 onward with roughly 2–8 hours effective latency, and a historical variant from 1999–2023. The paper reports better precipitation-detection scores than several global products across three regional radar networks and 36,678 quality-controlled stations, but these results have not been independently reproduced here. The product is openly licensed under CC BY 4.0 and explicitly is not an official warning product.
